In Naha's main market you can buy a fish downstairs and have it cooked upstairs a few minutes later. It's called mochiage, it's been running since 1990, and most first-time visitors walk straight past it 👇

🍱 Hungry yet? How it works, the market hours and where it is 👉 https://japanbystation.com/naha-where-to-stay-do-you-need-a-car

📌 SAVE THIS: HOW TO DO IT

1️⃣ Walk to the Makishi Public Market, about 10 minutes from Makishi or Miebashi monorail station, just off Kokusai-dori. It was rebuilt and reopened on the same spot in March 2023.

2️⃣ Choose fish, lobster or meat at one of the 75 shops on the ground floor, and pay for it there.

3️⃣ Ask the stallholder which upstairs restaurant suits what you bought. There are 12 eateries upstairs.

4️⃣ They cook it as sashimi, grilled or as a steak, and you pay a cooking fee to the restaurant. Add a drink or a bowl of soki soba while you wait.

💛 THE LITTLE EXTRA

Stallholders sometimes add a small something to your bag. In Okinawa that's called shiibun, and it's very much part of the market's charm.

⏰ WHEN

The market runs roughly 8:00 to 22:00, though each shop sets its own hours. The government's own write-up notes the upstairs places stay open fairly late, so it works as dinner too.
